decision.root_cause_hypothesis: The selection workflow relies on a noisy 16-sample Monte-Carlo estimate (robust_performance_mc) so estimator variance (relative to population spread: mean=0.4253, sd=0.0907) is causing misranking of candidates and unstable selection; this allows unsafe/zero-performing designs to survive and good designs to be displaced.
decision.rationale: Analyzer shows large estimator noise from the 16-sample robust_performance_mc (mean=0.4253, sd=0.0907) and several zero-scoring candidates; re-evaluating top candidates with higher-fidelity MC for elite selection should reduce misranking and stabilize progress without changing objective semantics.

proposed_change.guidance: Append persistent instruction to the Planner: After the population is scored using the default robust_performance_mc (16 samples), identify the top 10 candidates by the current composite score. Re-evaluate those top 10 using robust_performance_mc at higher fidelity (use 128 samples). For elite selection, archiving, and any elite_fraction copying, use the high-fidelity robust_performance_mc estimates (replace the 16-sample estimate). If fewer than 10 candidates exist, re-evaluate the top 25% rounded up. Continue normal low-cost scoring for the rest of the population to preserve throughput. Also, when a candidate's nominal_performance == 0 on nominal evaluation, treat it as clearly invalid (do not promote to elites) to avoid wasted re-evals.

decision.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Reduced misranking of contenders, more stable selection of genuinely robust designs, fewer regressions from noisy selection; should increase mean robust_performance_mc and reduce frequency of zero-performing elites. Also avoids wasting elite slots on nominally invalid designs.
decision.validation_plan_suggested_by_judge: The validator will run the next iteration with this Planner guidance in effect. Expected observable signal: an increase in population mean robust_performance_mc (and/or improved best robust_performance_mc) relative to the currently accepted state; reduced occurrence of zero-scoring candidates among elites. This intervention is low-risk and targets selection fidelity directly.
